title: Effects of Voiceover and Visual Elements on Viewers’ Assessment
author: Konrad Maj
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bau3ieyn

steps.title: Create base video
steps.instruction: Produce a 2.5‑minute video by professional journalists that includes a voice‑over narration about a fictional mayoral candidate; place the fictional TV‑station logo (“Regionalna TV”) in the upper‑right corner, add opening graphic credits “Political roulette”, and author credits at the end; show the male protagonist in scenes (desk, phone call, street walk) and include three additional speakers (two men, one woman) using fictitious names; set the story in a fictitious city and frame the report as a short TV news piece covering competence, morality, and sociability.

steps.title: Design thematic tickers
steps.instruction: Create eight “updating” tickers containing positive and negative statements that map onto the three dimensions (competence, morality, sociability), e.g., “a weak sportsman” vs. “a good sportsman”.

steps.title: Select photos for tickers
steps.instruction: From public image databases, pre‑select five photos for each of the eight tickers; have two independent assessors each identify two sets of photos that are equivalent in content and evoked emotion; retain the six tickers for which both assessors agree on the most appropriate photos (e.g., a fallen athlete for “weak sportsman”, a triumphant smiling athlete for “good sportsman”).

steps.title: Add visual add‑ons
steps.instruction: For each experimental condition, embed either a ticker or a selected image (never both simultaneously) into the video; display the visual element for approximately 5 seconds before it disappears.

steps.title: Assign participants and present video
steps.instruction: Randomly assign subjects to one of the 15 experimental conditions (including three control conditions); have participants wear a headset and watch the prepared video on a computer screen.

steps.title: Collect questionnaire data
steps.instruction: After viewing, give participants a questionnaire that: (1) rates the politician on competence, morality, and sociability on 1‑to‑7 scales; (2) rates six semantic‑differential items related to the visual add‑on content (e.g., weak vs. good sportsman, bad vs. good student) also on 1‑to‑7 scales.
